The Republic of the Councils of the Poor

Long have the Shepherds of the Romans been oppressed in the former lands of Dacia. Forced higher and higher into the mountains to survive the invaders, we have nevertheless survived into the present. However, with the spectre of nationalism looming over Europe, it might not be long before the last vestiges of the Roman Legions this far east are extinguished. Now is time to reclaim our heritage - now is time to clamour to the world: I am of the blood of Trajan!

It is clear that with the changing landscape around us, it is only a matter of time before some power or other decides to make a province of us. There is no other alternative than to gather the members of our League and form a new, more coherent union - the shaky foundation of a new Albanian state.

The old clans still dominate the political landscape of our country. A law finds itself ignored in Thopia domains. Recruits go missing in Gropaj lands. Mirdita estates barely pay their dues. Do they not see that the future of Albania is at stake? Through clever manipulation, exploitation of rivalries and precise application of force, we must rid Albania of the dominance of its old tribal elite.

Our control over Lake Shkoder in the north is troubled by bellicose neighbors who could launch raids across the border at any time. It is imperative that our fledgling state be given the security it needs. We must thus seize advance points on the approach from Herzegovina and deny sea access by taking the port of Cattaro. Surely the great powers must understand that this is strictly for our safety!

Down in Greece lives a sizeable group of our kinsmen, whom the locals call the Arvanites. Slowly, they are being assimilated - their language fading, their customs blending with the locals, their attachment slowly becoming dangerous to Albania. We must unite all Albanians - and liberate them before its too late!

As our country newly centralizes, the issue of the capital city is raised. There are a few options being proposed, each with its benefits and drawbacks. A port town like Durres, Vlore or even Shkoder would be beneficial for trade and could expand greatly, but would be vulnerable to invasions. Kruje is populous and has a central location, but is also poorly defensible. A different option would be build a new capital in the more defensible hills of the inland - a suitable place would be to expand the village of Tirana, not far from Diber.
